builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MoE Proxy Models for Low-Cost Failure Reproduction and Diagnosis in LLM RL Post-Training
summary: Replaces reproducing post-training RL failures on a large MoE model with a smaller proxy built by cluster-based expert pruning that preserves the backbone, routing, and basic capabilities. Constructing and validating the proxy takes work, and failures depending on scale or removed experts may not transfer. The target use is debugging training on Ascend platforms with dozens of NPUs, rather than small-scale inference.
rationale: The savings apply to operators of large MoE post-training RL clusters, outside the reader's infrastructure and budget.
technique: Pruned MoE proxies for reproducing RL failures

claims.statement: Replaces reproducing post-training RL failures on a large MoE model with a smaller proxy built by cluster-based expert pruning that preserves the backbone, routing, and basic capabilities. Constructing and validating the proxy takes work, and failures depending on scale or removed experts may not transfer. The target use is debugging training on Ascend platforms with dozens of NPUs, rather than small-scale inference.
Reports 50%-87.5% fewer accelerators and up to 33.3x lower NPU-hour cost per step while preserving training dynamics and reproducing failures of the original model.
